title: Services and Pod Connectivity

header.html: Understand connectivity between Pods; Use ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer service types and endpoints

toc.title: Endpoints: what a Service actually points at
How Services work on the node (short)
A fast way to test connectivity

html:
1The networking rules of Kubernetes

  1. Every Pod gets its own IP address. Pods can reach every other Pod by IP, on any node, without NAT (unless a NetworkPolicy blocks it).
  2. Nodes can reach all Pods and Pods can reach all nodes.
  3. Pod IPs are not stable: a replaced Pod gets a new IP. A Service gives a stable virtual IP and name in front of a changing set of Pods.
  4. The CNI plugin (Module 1) builds the Pod network; kube-proxy on each node turns Service IPs into Pod IPs.

Find IPs and nodes: k get pods -o wide. One Pod's IP: k get pod p -o jsonpath='{.status.podIP}'.

2Service types

Type Reachable from How Use
ClusterIP (default) inside the cluster virtual IP + DNS name internal services
NodePort outside via <any node IP>:<nodePort> opens the same port (30000-32767 by default) on every node, on top of a ClusterIP simple external access, tests
LoadBalancer outside via a cloud address asks the cloud for a load balancer; builds on NodePort production on a cloud
ExternalName inside DNS alias (CNAME) to an outside host; no proxy, no selector pointing at an external database
Headless (clusterIP: None) inside DNS returns Pod IPs directly StatefulSets

A Service has a selector (which Pods) and ports:

Field Meaning
port the port clients use on the Service
targetPort the port on the Pod's container (defaults to port)
nodePort the port opened on every node (NodePort and LoadBalancer only) 
k expose deployment shop --port=8080 --target-port=80                  # ClusterIP
k expose deployment web --name=web-np --port=80 --type=NodePort        # NodePort (random node port)
k expose pod server --port=80                                          # Service for a Pod
k create service externalname legacy-db --external-name=db.example.com
k expose deployment front --name=front-lb --port=80 --type=LoadBalancer
  • k expose copies the selector from the object it exposes and names the Service after it unless --name is given.
  • To choose a node port, generate YAML with --dry-run=client -o yaml, add nodePort: 30080 under the port, and apply (Lab 7.2).
  • In the lab cluster, a LoadBalancer Service never gets an external address (<pending>) because there is no cloud. On the exam, cloud behavior depends on the environment; the Service definition is what you create.

3Endpoints: what a Service actually points at

A Service sends traffic only to Ready Pods that match its selector. The list of those Pod IPs is held in EndpointSlice objects (the older Endpoints object still exists but is deprecated).

k get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=db
k get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=db -o jsonpath='{range .items[*].endpoints[*]}{.addresses[0]}{"\n"}{end}'
k get endpoints db                      # older view, still printed

No endpoints = the Service cannot work. The three causes, in order of frequency:

  1. The Service selector does not match the Pod labels (a typo; Lab 7.3).
  2. The Pods are not Ready (failing readiness probe, crash loop).
  3. targetPort is wrong: endpoints exist but connections are refused.

Debug in this order: k get svc,endpointslices, k get pods --show-labels, k describe svc, then k exec into a client Pod and wget -qO- -T3 http://svc.

4Service DNS names

CoreDNS gives every Service a name: <service>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local.

From Works
same namespace shop
other namespace shop.svc1 or the full name

A Pod's /etc/resolv.conf has a search path (<ns>.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local) and nameserver set to the DNS Service IP. Services get the A record; headless Services return every Pod IP; StatefulSet Pods get pod-0.service.ns.svc.cluster.local. Cross-namespace access needs only the right name (Lab 7.7). More on DNS in Module 8.

5How Services work on the node (short)

kube-proxy watches Services and EndpointSlices and writes rules (iptables, IPVS or nftables mode) so that traffic to the ClusterIP is randomly forwarded to one ready Pod IP. The ClusterIP is virtual: it is not on any interface, so you cannot ping it; test with the Service port using wget/curl. If Service traffic fails on one node only, check that node's kube-proxy Pod (Module 13).

6A fast way to test connectivity

k run tmp --rm -i --restart=Never --image=busybox:1.36 -- wget -qO- -T3 http://shop.svc1:8080
k -n front exec client -- wget -qO- -T3 http://server.back

--rm -i --restart=Never runs a throw-away Pod and removes it. -T3 makes wget give up after 3 seconds so a blocked path fails quickly.

7Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m07 -->

Lab 7.1: clusterip service

Domain: Networking | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m07-01-clusterip-service)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace svc1, the Deployment shop (2 replicas, nginx:alpine, listening on port 80) exists. Create a Service named shop of type ClusterIP that is reachable inside the cluster on port 8080 and forwards to the containers' port 80.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n svc1 expose deployment shop --port=8080 --target-port=80
kubectl -n svc1 get svc shop

Lab 7.2: nodeport service

Domain: Networking | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m07-02-nodeport-service)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace svc2, expose the Deployment web (nginx on port 80) with a Service named web-np of type NodePort, service port 80, using the fixed node port 30080.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n svc2 expose deployment web --name=web-np --port=80 --type=NodePort --dry-run=client -o yaml > /tmp/web-np.yaml
sed -i 's/  - port: 80/  - port: 80\n    nodePort: 30080/' /tmp/web-np.yaml
kubectl -n svc2 apply -f /tmp/web-np.yaml
kubectl -n svc2 get svc web-np

Lab 7.3: fix service selector

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m07-03-fix-service-selector)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace svc3, the Service api does not work: requests to http://api.svc3 hang. The Deployment api (2 replicas) is healthy. Find the cause and fix the Service without changing the Deployment, so that http://api.svc3 returns the nginx welcome page.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n svc3 get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=api
kubectl -n svc3 get svc api -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'; echo
kubectl -n svc3 get pods --show-labels
kubectl -n svc3 patch svc api -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"api"}}}'

Lab 7.4: endpoint ips

Domain: Networking | Points: 4 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m07-04-endpoint-ips)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace svc4, the Service db is backed by several Pods. Write the IP addresses of all Pods that currently serve the Service (one IP per line, sorted) to ~/answers/endpoints.txt on the host.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n svc4 get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=db
kubectl -n svc4 get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=db -o jsonpath='{range .items[*].endpoints[*]}{.addresses[0]}{"\n"}{end}' | sort > ~/answers/endpoints.txt

Lab 7.5: loadbalancer service

Domain: Networking | Points: 4 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m07-05-loadbalancer-service)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace svc5, expose the Deployment front (nginx, port 80) with a Service named front-lb of type LoadBalancer on port 80. In this test cluster there is no cloud load balancer, so the external address stays pending; only the Service definition is checked.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n svc5 expose deployment front --name=front-lb --port=80 --type=LoadBalancer
kubectl -n svc5 get svc front-lb

Lab 7.6: externalname

Domain: Networking | Points: 4 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m07-06-externalname)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace svc6, create a Service named legacy-db that makes the name legacy-db.svc6.svc.cluster.local resolve (as a DNS alias) to the external host db.example.com.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n svc6 create service externalname legacy-db --external-name=db.example.com
kubectl -n svc6 get svc legacy-db

Lab 7.7: cross namespace dns

Domain: Networking | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m07-07-cross-namespace-dns)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

The Pod server (nginx) runs in the namespace back and the Pod client (busybox) runs in the namespace front. Make the client able to fetch the nginx page from the server by the name http://server.back (do not touch the Pods). Then write the full DNS name of the Service (including .svc.cluster.local) to ~/answers/fqdn.txt.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n back expose pod server --port=80
kubectl -n front exec client -- wget -qO- -T3 http://server.back | head -3
echo server.back.svc.cluster.local > ~/answers/fqdn.txt

Lab 7.8: multiport service

Domain: Networking | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m07-08-multiport-service)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace svc8, the Deployment app (2 replicas) has Pods that listen on port 80 (web) and 8080 (metrics; the image is nginx so only 80 answers, the definition is what counts). Create a Service named app that exposes two named ports: http on port 80 targeting container port 80, and metrics on port 9090 targeting container port 8080.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n svc8 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: app}
spec:
  selector: {app: app}
  ports:
  - {name: http, port: 80, targetPort: 80}
  - {name: metrics, port: 9090, targetPort: 8080}
Y
kubectl -n svc8 get svc app

<!-- /LABS -->

8Recall questions

R1Which two properties of Pod IPs make a Service necessary?

Show the answer

Pod IPs change when Pods are replaced, and a workload has many Pods; a Service gives one stable name and IP.

R2What is the difference between port and targetPort?

Show the answer

port is what clients use on the Service; targetPort is the container port traffic is sent to.

R3Which node port range is the default for NodePort Services?

Show the answer

30000 to 32767.

R4A Service has no endpoints. What do you check first?

Show the answer

That the Service selector matches the Pod labels (k get pods --show-labels), then that the Pods are Ready.

R5Which Service type creates a DNS alias to an outside host?

Show the answer

ExternalName.

R6What is the full DNS name of Service api in namespace prod?

Show the answer

api.prod.svc.cluster.local.

R7Why does ping <ClusterIP> fail even when the Service works?

Show the answer

The ClusterIP is virtual (kube-proxy rules); only the Service ports answer.

R8Which object holds the Pod IPs behind a Service?

Show the answer

EndpointSlices (older Endpoints is deprecated).

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Types ClusterIP, NodePort (30000-32767), LoadBalancer, ExternalName, headless
Expose k expose ... --port --target-port --type --name
Endpoints k get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=<svc>; empty = selector, readiness or port problem
DNS <svc>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local; <svc>.<ns> from another namespace
Test busybox wget -qO- -T3 http://svc from a Pod
Pod network every Pod has an IP; Pods reach Pods without NAT
